title_clean: The Opportunities that Benefit Option Buyers
summary: Tells the Thales of Miletus olive-press story as history's first option purchase, then argues option buying is viable only with genuine predictive skill, citing a 25-year Nifty monthly-chart seasonality study and executing a put-financed bullish call trade into April expiry.
lessons: Option buying rewards demonstrated predictive skill; without it, time decay makes buying a losing business.
Thales of Miletus (booking olive presses with a token advance) is history's first recorded option purchase.
Study of 25 years of Nifty monthly charts: falls rarely last 3 straight months (only two 4-month streaks), and a rally reliably followed.
A directional call buy can be financed by selling a lower put; capping with a short call at strong resistance reduces cost further.
SEBI-type studies: roughly 90% of F&O traders lose; only ~1% earn meaningful profits.

strategies.name: Put-financed directional call (bull call financed by short put)
strategies.construction: Buy near-ATM monthly call (17,800/18,000CE); finance by selling an equal lower strike put (16,800/17,000PE); optionally cap by selling an OTM call (18,200CE) at major resistance
strategies.numbers: Entered on a 70-80 point dip; closed profitable within days; 18,200CE cap chosen at stated April resistance
strategies.best_regime: Strong post-correction bullish conviction with a defined downside shelf
strategies.adjustments: Book entirely once momentum confirms; re-strike higher with the same financing structure
strategies.risks: Both legs lose if market breaks the put strike; uncapped version has full short-put downside
